narrative.overview:
VeriDoc is a case file on soft paper. An analyst or MLRO reads for long stretches, often projected for a panel, so the ground is a warm grey-cream (never white, nothing above 97% lightness), text is ink-blue near-black, and one muted ink blue carries action, selection and AI proposals. Status is desaturated sage, ochre, rust and wine and always arrives with a word or an icon. The world is flat: hairline borders, 4px corners, no gradients, no glass, almost no shadow.

Its signature is structural honesty. A lead is set as two columns: the agent's proposal in prose on the left, and beside it, divided by one strong vertical rule, a ruled ledger of what code established with a state mark. Anything explained goes quiet: a dashed, transparent receipt rather than a card. Open sections get a strong underline rule and 18px headings; everything else folds.

Light is the default. Dark is an opt-in (`data-theme="dark"`), retuned to the same hues (ink blue lifted to 78% lightness, paper at 11%) and never the default.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper ground, ink-blue text, a single ink-blue accent
Hairline rules do the work that shadows and fills do elsewhere
Prose for agent claims, ledger (label / value rows) for code facts
Mono only for ids, amounts, dates and check ids, with tabular figures
Collapsed folds for audit material; the verdict reads first

rules.name: The Word Beside The Colour Rule
rules.body: Status colour never stands alone: a pill carries a dot and a word, a state mark carries an icon and a label.

rules.name: The Not Blinding Rule
rules.body: No surface is above 97% lightness; a white PDF is multiplied onto the paper tone (`mix-blend-mode: multiply`; dark theme dims it instead) so the document pane is not a lamp.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Ink blue is the only hue for action and selection. Amber means AWS and nothing else.

rules.name: The Mono Is For Data Rule
rules.body: Mono is used only for ids, amounts, dates and check ids (`.mono`, `code`, `kbd`, counts). Names and sentences stay in the reading face; a fact value is mono only when its key is on the id/amount/date list.

rules.name: The Verbatim Terms Rule
rules.body: Banking terms and check ids appear exactly as the data gives them; amounts format as `SGD 18,530.00`.

rules.name: The Flat At Rest Rule
rules.body: Cards, leads and findings carry no shadow. Only overlays and the document sheet may.

rules.name: The Quiet Receipt Rule
rules.body: What is resolved goes dashed, transparent and muted (explained findings, withheld leads, off notes); what needs attention stays solid on surface.

dos: Do set agent claims as prose and code-established facts as a ruled ledger in a separate column; separate them structurally, not by a pill alone.
Do pair every status colour with a word or icon.
Do keep every surface within the paper range (lightness at or below 97%) and use hairline borders instead of shadows.
Do use 4px corners everywhere except filter chips.
Do set ids, amounts, dates and check ids in Geist Mono with tabular figures, and leave everything else in Hanken Grotesk.
Do make resolved items quiet (dashed, transparent) and collapse audit material behind folds.
Do retune dark mode to the same hues; light stays the default.
donts: Don't put a decision-looking surface on an AI output; leads are proposals and the one primary action remains Record decision.
Don't use pure white, gradients, glass or hard offset shadows.
Don't use colour as the only carrier of meaning, or amber for anything but AWS.
Don't use mono for names or prose, or uppercase tracked labels.
Don't stack same-weight sections with the answer far down; the verdict leads.
